newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease 0.32 pct in sharply lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease 0.32 pct in sharply lower volume.

text.p: Istanbul stocks dropped slightly in profit-taking on Tuesday after the recent sharp gains fuelled by hopes ahead of the Monday approval of the new secularist coalition government, brokers said.
Brokers said a correction was awaited today but the market kept up its political hopes that the new government will win a forthcoming confidence vote in parliament.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,851, down six points or 0.32 percent from Monday's all-time high close of 1,857. It rose 2.31 percent yesterday on top of last week's 10.5 percent surge.
Trade volume was more than halved to 24.76 trillion lira ($166.5 million) from Monday's 53.02 trillion ($357.4 million).

"The index moved in a tight margin today with selective activity. I expect volume and trend to improve tomorrow because there was a late recovery today. The index will probably drift sideways until the confidence vote," said Zuhal Topaloglu from Ekinciler securities.
The secularist coalition of conservative leader Mesut Yilmaz who officially became the new prime minister after Demirel's approval of his cabinet on Monday, will face a confidence vote on July 12.
Yilmaz's alliance is a minority coalition of two right and one left-wing parties, supported by another left-wing party.
